_notes: Locally added -- upstream pinmame-nvram-maps has no map for Avatar.
Every address here was found by watching an automated 4-player game rather than by reading
values out of a capture: the ALP4K was driven through its own streamer, so nothing was typed in
off the display and nothing had to be trusted.
current_player and current_ball are adjacent bytes in CPU RAM at 0x000384A8 and 0x000384A9,
player low and ball high -- the shape every Stern SAM game checked uses. The player byte
completed 1->2->3 three times, once per ball; the ball byte once.
Scores are 4 bytes on 8-byte centres from 0x021109E4, the only group of four evenly spaced
values that rose monotonically through the game. Same base as 24, X-Men and twd_156c, and the
same 8-byte spacing as 24 -- but that is coincidence, not inheritance: the base and stride are
per-ROM across every SAM game measured.
player_count at 0x02110900, the one address shared by every SAM game checked.
High score records are 0x20 apart from 0x02102A38 with NUL-terminated initials at +0x00, a
4-byte score at +0x18 and a 16-bit checksum in the last two bytes of the first 30. Six records
pass that check and the seventh does not, which is what bounds the block.
The first five hold Stern's factory ladder (75M/55M/40M/30M/25M with 'G S'/'L R'/'J R'/'D T'/
'P P'). The sixth is the Final Battle Champion, read off the machine's own DMD: after game over
it cycles every champion entry, which is where a record's name comes from -- no amount of NVRAM
analysis will give it.
Only avr_200 is claimed; SAM addresses move between revisions.
Confirmed after the fact: exiting the table wrote the .nv, and the map decodes that 4-player
game as 4 players scoring 1,767,130 / 1,360,920 / 976,890 / 1,006,410, with all six checksum
regions valid. Every address here was found by behaviour and then checked against the result.
game_over, tilted and credits come from a 1,097-frame recording of live memory spanning an
operator-menu session and a full game with a tilt on ball 1. The same session promoted
indices 30 and 32 exactly as the free_play-relative rule predicted.
0x000384DA is the same status bitfield trn_174h uses, at the same offset from the ball counter
(+0x31): 1 in attract on both sides of the game, 19 while playing, 21 for exactly the nineteen
samples between the tilt and the end of the tilted ball -- during which player 1's score sat
frozen at 110,240. game_over decodes with mask 0x12 inverted, correct in all 1,097 frames, and
tilted is bit 0x04. Note the same offset held an unrelated five-valued byte on st_162h, so this
shape recurs but cannot be assumed.
credits at 0x0211100C, the fifth SAM game measured at that same address: rose to 2 with six
coins at three a credit, fell to 1 at game start.
